newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kemira targets 16 pct ROE long-term -CEO.
newsitem.headline: Kemira targets 16 pct ROE long-term -CEO.

text.p: Finnish chemicals group Kemira Oy aims for a 16 percent return on equity in the longer term, Kemira CEO and Chairman Heimo Karinen said on Monday.
"We are aiming for... a 16 percent return on equity (ROE)," Karinen told a news conference after the company's results, adding that the group's 1996 ROE was 14 percent.
Asked when the group would achieve the goal, he said this would be as soon as possible but the objective was longer term.
Kemira also aims to boost real annual net sales growth to five percent after just one percent growth in 1996, he said.
With 1996 gearing at 49 percent, the company was within its gearing ratio target of 30 to 50 percent, he said.

"I don't see any reason why Kemira should not continue to develop favourably... Analysts are betting on an improvement in profits, and they have fairly good expertise," Karinen said in response to a question on Kemira's earnings prospects for 1997.

Kemira reported a record 1996 profit before extraordinary items and taxes of 851 million markka, up from 718 million in 1995, despite operating losses of 21 million in its pigments unit, where sales were dented by weak titanium dioxide prices.
"The potential for pigments is positive, but the pigments unit's result for this year will not yet be satisfactory," Karinen said.

"I hope it will not be loss-making (this year)," he said of the unit. Kemira has broadened the product range of its Dutch (pigments) unit, and will be able to adjust production levels there better in the future, Karinen said.
